questions.q: Why isn't locking down storage access (RBAC, ACLs, bucket policies) enough governance on its own?
options: Because storage locked down this way becomes permanently unreadable even to admins
Because people still need a way to discover that a dataset exists and understand what's in it, which access control alone doesn't provide
Because RBAC and ACLs don't actually restrict anyone from reading data
Because data catalogs are required before any storage account can be created
questions.explain: Locking down access controls who CAN read data, but doesn't help legitimate users discover what data exists, what it contains, or who owns it — that's the catalog's job.

questions.q: In Microsoft Purview, what does registering a data source actually do?
options: Tells Purview the source exists and which collection it belongs to — it does not extract any metadata yet
Deletes the source from its original storage account
Grants every Purview user read access to the underlying data
Immediately scans the entire source and classifies every column
questions.explain: Registration is a lightweight step that just makes Purview aware of the source and its collection. Metadata extraction happens in a separate scan.

questions.q: What does a Purview scan actually do that registration does not?
options: Removes the source from its collection
Only renames the source in the catalog UI
Creates the storage account for the first time
Walks the registered source, extracts schema and file metadata, and can apply classification rules to flag sensitive columns
questions.explain: Scanning is the step that actually extracts real, searchable metadata from a registered source, optionally applying classification rules as it goes.

questions.q: What is a Purview 'collection' roughly analogous to?
options: A hierarchy for organizing sources and scoping permissions, similar in spirit to how resource groups organize Azure resources
A storage account's access tier
A single scanned table inside a database
An IAM role in AWS
questions.explain: Collections organize sources and scope permissions within Purview, conceptually similar to how resource groups organize and scope Azure resources.

questions.q: What is the rough AWS equivalent of a Microsoft Purview 'scan'?
options: An S3 bucket policy
An AWS Lake Formation grant
An IAM access boundary
An AWS Glue crawler
questions.explain: A Glue crawler plays the same role as a Purview scan: it walks a data source and populates the catalog with real schema and metadata.
